docs.title: mallops
docs.text:
Modular MLOps in Rust — from data ingestion to edge devices, one block at a time.

Early stage

mallops is in the design phase. The specification and architecture are open for feedback.

docs.title: Why mallops
docs.text:
• Every MLOps step is a block — ingestion, storage, preprocessing, training, model engineering, evaluation, packaging, versioning, deploy, serving, monitoring, retrain. Add, remove or replace any of them.
  • Bring any model, any library — ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle, GGUF, XGBoost, your own format.
  • Three ways to use it — Rust library, plugins (WASM or external processes in any language), or standalone with YAML and the mallops CLI.
  • Edge-ready — local serving, distributed monitoring and federated learning on devices.
  • Reproducible — content-addressed artifacts, lineage for every run, cached re-runs.
flowchart LR
    I[Ingest] --> S[(Data storage)] --> P[Preprocess] --> T[Train] --> E[Evaluate]
    E -->|gate| K[Package] --> V[Version] --> D[Deploy] --> SV[Serve]
    SV --> M[Monitor] -->|drift| R[Retrain] --> T
    D --> EDGE[Edge devices] -. federated updates .-> T

docs.title: mallops — Architecture
docs.text: Companion to SPEC.md. Decisions are recorded in adr/.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph User
        Y[mallops.yaml]
        L[Rust code]
    end
    subgraph Core["mallops-core"]
        P[Config parser + validator]
        G[DAG builder]
        R[Runtime / scheduler]
        REG[Block registry]
        S[(ArtifactStore trait<br/>local · memory)]
        LIN[Lineage events<br/>JSON sink]
    end
    subgraph Backends["Optional backends"]
        RS3[(S3 / GCS / Azure)]
        LS[SQLite · OpenLineage · MLflow]
    end
    S -.-> RS3
    LIN -.-> LS
    subgraph Blocks
        STD[mallops-std<br/>feature-gated]
        RS[User Rust blocks]
        W[WASM components]
        X[External process<br/>gRPC / CLI]
    end
    Y --> P --> G --> R
    L --> G
    REG --> R
    R <--> S
    R --> LIN --> S
    STD & RS --> REG
    W & X --> REG

The core knows only three things: blocks, artifacts, and the graph between them. Everything ML-specific lives in blocks.

Store and lineage are not blocks: blocks are nodes of the DAG, while store and lineage act on every edge. The core owns their contracts and a minimal default; every real backend is optional (ADR-0006).

docs.title: 2. Workspace layout
docs.text:
mallops/
├── crates/
│   ├── mallops-core/   # traits, artifacts, store & lineage contracts, config, runtime
│   ├── mallops-cli/    # `mallops` binary              (v0.1)
│   ├── mallops-std/    # standard blocks, feature-gated (v0.1)
│   └── mallops-edge/   # edge agent + FL aggregator     (v0.4)
├── docs/
└── examples/

Crates are created only when implemented. Splitting mallops-std into per-stage crates is deferred until compile times or dependency weight demand it (ADR-0001).

Crate Depends on Heavy deps mallops-core — tokio, serde, blake3, tracing mallops-std core per feature: arrow, polars, linfa, ort, axum, object_store (store-s3, store-gcs, store-azure), rusqlite (lineage-sqlite), … mallops-cli core, std clap mallops-edge core, std (subset) tonic

docs.title: 3. Core abstractions
docs.text:
/// Static description of a block: identity, I/O ports, config schema.
pub struct BlockSpec {
    pub id: &'static str,            // "std/train.external"
    pub stage: Stage,                // Ingest, Preprocess, Train, …
    pub inputs: Vec<Port>,           // name + accepted kind/formats/flavors
    pub outputs: Vec<Port>,
    pub config_schema: schemars::Schema,
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait Block: Send + Sync {
    fn spec(&self) -> BlockSpec;
    async fn run(&self, ctx: &Context, inputs: Inputs) -> Result<Outputs>;
}

/// Given to each block during execution.
pub struct Context {
    pub run_id: RunId,
    pub workdir: PathBuf,            // scratch dir, also mounted for external blocks
    pub store: Arc<dyn ArtifactStore>,
    pub config: serde_json::Value,   // the block's `with:` section, already validated
    pub span: tracing::Span,
}
// Blocks never touch lineage: the runtime records it around `run()`.

pub struct Artifact {
    pub id: ArtifactId,              // BLAKE3 of manifest + payload
    pub manifest: Manifest,          // kind, format, flavor, signature, metadata, parents
}

Serving uses one more trait, implemented by backend crates/plugins and selected by flavor:

#[async_trait]
pub trait Predictor: Send + Sync {
    fn flavors(&self) -> &[&str];                       // e.g. ["onnx"], ["sklearn-pickle"]
    async fn load(&self, pkg: &Artifact, ctx: &Context) -> Result<Box<dyn Loaded>>;
}

No ML type appears in core signatures: tensors and dataframes are payload files or plugin-internal types. This is what keeps mallops library-agnostic (ADR-0004).

docs.title: 4. Execution model
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CLI
    participant Core as Runtime
    participant Store
    participant B as Block
    CLI->>Core: run(mallops.yaml)
    Core->>Core: parse, validate schemas & port compatibility, topo-sort
    loop each ready node (parallel when independent)
        Core->>Core: cache key = hash(block id, version, config, input artifact ids)
        alt cache hit
            Core->>Store: reuse outputs
        else
            Core->>B: run(ctx, inputs)
            B->>Store: put(payload, manifest)
            Store-->>B: ArtifactId
            B-->>Core: outputs
        end
        Core->>Core: emit lineage event → sinks
    end
    Core-->>CLI: run summary
  • Scheduler: tokio tasks, bounded concurrency (--jobs).
  • Failure: a failed node cancels its descendants; other branches finish. Re-running resumes from cache.
  • Quality gates are blocks that return an error (stop) or a skip signal for downstream nodes.

docs.title: 5. Plugin model
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    R[Runtime] --> N[Native Rust block<br/>compile-time, inventory]
    R --> W[WASM component<br/>wasmtime, sandboxed]
    R --> X[External process<br/>gRPC or CLI contract]
    X --> PY[Python / R / Julia / containers]
Kind Use when Isolation Overhead Native Rust, performance critical none zero WASM portable, untrusted, light compute strong low External other languages, GPUs, heavy frameworks process/container process spawn + IPC

The external CLI contract is the simplest: mallops writes inputs.json (artifact paths + manifests) and config.json into the workdir, runs the command, and collects files declared in outputs.json. Any language can implement it in a few lines. The gRPC variant adds long-lived workers and streaming. See ADR-0003.

docs.title: 6. Artifact store and lineage
docs.text:
Two kinds of "storage" exist and must not be confused:

Data storage blocks Artifact store What Persist user data to lakes, DBs, feature stores Hand artifacts from one block to the next Where in the DAG A node Every edge In the core No (mallops-std / plugins) Contract + local and memory impls Optional Yes The backend is; the mechanism is not

docs.title: 6.1 Artifact store
docs.text:
#[async_trait]
pub trait ArtifactStore: Send + Sync {
    async fn put(&self, manifest: Manifest, payload: &Path) -> Result<ArtifactId>;
    async fn get(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> Result<Artifact>;
    /// Materialize the payload locally (no-op for `local`, download for remote).
    async fn fetch(&self, id: &ArtifactId, dest: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf>;
    async fn exists(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> Result<bool>;
}
  • Core implementations: LocalStore (filesystem, default, ./.mallops) and MemoryStore (ephemeral; tests and throwaway runs).
  • Optional: ObjectStore adapter over the object_store crate (S3, GCS, Azure) behind mallops-std features; anything else as a plugin.
  • What depends on it: data hand-off between nodes and processes, caching (cache key → output ids), resume after failure, model registry (v0.2).
  • Layout: artifacts/<hash>/…, registry/<model>/<version>.json (v0.2).

docs.title: 6.2 Lineage
docs.text:
pub enum LineageEvent {
    RunStarted { run: RunId, pipeline_hash: Hash, git_commit: Option<String>, host: HostInfo },
    BlockStarted { run: RunId, node: String, block: BlockRef, config_hash: Hash, inputs: Vec<ArtifactId> },
    ArtifactProduced { run: RunId, node: String, artifact: ArtifactId },
    BlockFinished { run: RunId, node: String, status: Status, duration: Duration, cached: bool },
    RunFinished { run: RunId, status: Status },
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait LineageSink: Send + Sync {
    async fn record(&self, event: &LineageEvent) -> Result<()>;
}
  • The runtime is the only producer: it alone sees the whole graph. Blocks stay unaware of lineage.
  • Core sink: JsonSink, writing runs/<run-id>/lineage.json into the artifact store.
  • Optional sinks: SQLite (queryable), OpenLineage (Marquez, DataHub…), MLflow — mallops-std features or plugins.
  • Zero or more sinks; lineage: off disables it. A failing sink logs a warning and never fails the run.
  • Caching does not depend on lineage: it uses artifact hashes in the store.

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|HTTP/gRPC| S[mallops serve]
    S --> T[Preprocess transform<br/>from package]
    T --> P{Predictor by flavor}
    P --> O[ort]
    P --> TR[tract]

docs.title: 8. Edge and federated learning (v0.4)
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph Cloud
        AGG[FL aggregator]
        REGI[Model registry]
        COL[Metrics collector]
    end
    subgraph Edge["Edge node (mallops-edge)"]
        SV[Local serving]
        LT[Local training]
        BUF[Metrics buffer]
    end
    REGI -- signed model pull --> SV
    AGG -- global weights --> LT
    LT -- weight deltas only --> AGG
    SV --> BUF -- push when online --> COL
    COL -- drift alert --> RT[Retrain trigger]
  • Transport: gRPC (tonic) with mTLS; nodes initiate connections (NAT-friendly).
  • Aggregation strategies are blocks (FedAvg default); privacy techniques plug in at the aggregator.
  • Model weights exchanged in whatever format the flavor defines; the aggregator delegates averaging to a flavor-aware plugin.

docs.title: 9. Cross-cutting concerns
docs.text: Concern Choice Errors thiserror in libraries, anyhow only in the CLI Logging/tracing tracing; OpenTelemetry exporter behind a feature Config serde + serde_yaml + schemars Async tokio CLI clap derive Testing unit tests per crate, integration tests running example pipelines, insta snapshots for CLI output

docs.title: mallops — Technical Specification
docs.text: Status: Draft · Target: v0.1 · Last update: 2026-11-21

docs.title: 1. Vision
docs.text:
mallops is a modular MLOps framework written in Rust. It covers the whole machine-learning lifecycle — from data ingestion to serving, monitoring and retraining, down to edge devices with federated learning — through composable blocks.

It can be used in three ways, all backed by the same core:

Mode Who How Library Rust developers depend on mallops-core, implement Block, compose pipelines in code Plugins anyone, any language ship a block as a WASM component or as an external process speaking the mallops gRPC protocol Standalone ML engineers, ops describe a pipeline in mallops.yaml, run it with the mallops CLI, add/remove blocks without writing code

docs.title: 1.1 Design principles
docs.text:
1. Format and library agnostic. mallops never imposes a model format, a data format or an ML library. An artifact is opaque files + a manifest. ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle, GGUF, XGBoost JSON, a custom binary — all first-class.
  2. Everything is a block. Every lifecycle step, including storage, deploy and retrain triggers, is a replaceable block with declared inputs and outputs.
  3. Small core, optional everything else. The core has no ML dependency. Standard blocks live behind Cargo feature flags.
  4. Reproducible by default. Content-addressed artifacts, locked configs, recorded seeds and environment.
  5. Local first, scale out later. A full pipeline runs on a laptop with zero infrastructure; the same pipeline targets object storage, remote runners and edge fleets by swapping blocks.

docs.title: 1.2 Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not a container orchestrator (it can call Kubernetes, Nomad, Docker as deploy blocks).
  • Not a deep-learning framework (it wraps burn, candle, PyTorch, scikit-learn, …).
  • Not a data warehouse or feature store (it integrates with them via blocks).
  • No GUI in v1 (a dashboard may come as a separate project).

docs.title: 2. Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Block Unit of work with typed inputs, outputs and config. Implements the Block trait (or the plugin protocol). Stage Lifecycle category a block belongs to (ingest, preprocess, train, …). Used for docs, validation hints and CLI listing — not enforced ordering. Artifact Immutable output of a block: a set of files plus a manifest, identified by its content hash. Pipeline DAG of block instances wired by artifact references, defined in YAML or code. Run One execution of a pipeline; has an id, a lineage record and logs. Flavor Tag in a model manifest telling which loader/predictor can use it (e.g. onnx, torchscript, sklearn-pickle, gguf, custom:acme). Artifact store Internal storage through which blocks exchange artifacts. Contract in the core, backends pluggable. Not to be confused with data storage blocks. Lineage sink Pluggable destination of the lineage events emitted by the runtime (JSON file, SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow…). Plugin Block distributed outside the mallops binary (Rust crate, WASM component, or external process). Edge node Device running mallops-edge: local serving, local metrics, optional federated training.

docs.title: 3. Functional requirements
docs.text: Each stage below lists what the standard library of blocks (mallops-std) must offer and what the core must make possible. Anything not covered can be added as a plugin.

docs.title: 3.1 Data ingestion
docs.text:
• FR-ING-1: read from local files (CSV, JSON/NDJSON, Parquet, arbitrary files) — v0.1.
  • FR-ING-2: read from HTTP(S) and object stores (S3, GCS, Azure) — v0.2.
  • FR-ING-3: read from databases (PostgreSQL, SQLite) and streams (Kafka, MQTT) — v0.3+.
  • FR-ING-4: optional schema validation; ingest is incremental when the source supports it.

docs.title: 3.2 Data storage
docs.text:
Two distinct concerns, deliberately kept apart (ADR-0006):

a) Data storage blocks — persisting user data to external systems is an ordinary, optional stage. - FR-STO-1: blocks that write datasets/features to object stores, data lakes (Delta, Iceberg), databases and feature stores — v0.2+.

b) Artifact store — the internal mechanism through which blocks hand artifacts to each other. Not a block: it sits on every edge of the DAG. - FR-STO-2: the core defines the ArtifactStore contract and ships two minimal implementations: local (filesystem, default) and memory (ephemeral, for tests and throwaway runs) — v0.1. - FR-STO-3: remote backends (S3, GCS, Azure, …) are optional (mallops-std features or plugins) — v0.2. - FR-STO-4: content addressing (BLAKE3) — identical content is stored once; enables caching and resume. - FR-STO-5: garbage collection of artifacts unreachable from retained runs — v0.2.

docs.title: 3.3 Preprocessing (data → features)
docs.text:
• FR-PRE-1: tabular transforms (select, filter, impute, scale, encode, split) on Arrow data — v0.1.
  • FR-PRE-2: user-defined transforms (Rust closure, WASM, external process).
  • FR-PRE-3: fitted transforms are themselves artifacts, so serving reuses the exact same preprocessing.

docs.title: 3.4 Training
docs.text:
• FR-TRN-1: native Rust training (linfa for classic ML) — v0.1.
  • FR-TRN-2: deep learning via burn/candle — v0.3.
  • FR-TRN-3: external trainer: run any command/container (Python, R, Julia…) that reads input artifacts and writes outputs into a mallops-managed workspace directory — v0.1. This is how PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, XGBoost are supported without Rust bindings.
  • FR-TRN-4: hyperparameters, seed and environment recorded in the run lineage.

docs.title: 3.5 Model engineering
docs.text:
• FR-ENG-1: hyperparameter search (grid, random; Bayesian as plugin) as a block that fans out training sub-runs — v0.2.
  • FR-ENG-2: post-training transforms as blocks: quantization, pruning, format conversion (e.g. torch → onnx) — delegated to the relevant tool.

docs.title: 3.6 Model evaluation
docs.text:
• FR-EVL-1: standard metrics (accuracy, precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE, MAE, R²) — v0.1.
  • FR-EVL-2: quality gates: a pipeline can fail or branch when a metric is below a threshold or worse than the current production model.
  • FR-EVL-3: custom metrics via plugins.

docs.title: 3.7 Model packaging
docs.text:
• FR-PKG-1: package = model artifact + preprocessing artifacts + manifest (flavor, signature, requirements) — v0.1.
  • FR-PKG-2: optional OCI image output for serving — v0.2.
  • FR-PKG-3: artifact signing (Sigstore/cosign or ed25519) — v0.3.

docs.title: 3.8 Model versioning
docs.text:
• FR-VER-1: model registry backed by the artifact store: name → versions → stages (staging, production, archived) — v0.2.
  • FR-VER-2: every version links to the run lineage that produced it (data hashes, code version, config).

docs.title: 3.9 Deploy
docs.text:
• FR-DEP-1: deploy targets as blocks: local process, Docker, Kubernetes manifest, SSH host, edge fleet — v0.2+.
  • FR-DEP-2: strategies: replace, canary, shadow — v0.3.
  • FR-DEP-3: rollback to a previous registry version in one command.

docs.title: 3.10 Model serving
docs.text:
• FR-SRV-1: HTTP/JSON inference server (mallops serve) — v0.1.
  • FR-SRV-2: gRPC endpoint, batching, health/readiness probes — v0.2.
  • FR-SRV-3: backend-agnostic: the server dispatches to a Predictor chosen by the package flavor (ort, tract, candle, burn, linfa, llama.cpp, external Python process…).

docs.title: 3.11 Monitoring and logging
docs.text:
• FR-MON-1: structured logs (tracing) for every run and every request — v0.1.
  • FR-MON-2: Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces — v0.3.
  • FR-MON-3: data/prediction drift detection (PSI, KS test) as blocks — v0.3.

docs.title: 3.12 Retrain
docs.text:
• FR-RET-1: triggers as blocks: schedule (cron), drift alert, new data, manual — v0.3.
  • FR-RET-2: a trigger starts a pipeline run; evaluation gates decide promotion.

docs.title: 3.13 Edge
docs.text:
• FR-EDG-1: mallops-edge agent: single static binary, cross-compiled for aarch64/armv7/x86_64 — v0.4.
  • FR-EDG-2: local serving with any Predictor backend, offline-capable.
  • FR-EDG-3: distributed monitoring: nodes buffer metrics/drift stats locally and push them when connected.
  • FR-EDG-4: federated learning: central aggregator (FedAvg, FedProx as plugin), nodes train locally, only model updates leave the device; optional secure aggregation and differential privacy as plugins.
  • FR-EDG-5: fleet deploy: pull-based model updates with signature verification.

docs.title: 3.14 Lineage
docs.text:
• FR-LIN-1: the runtime emits lineage events (RunStarted, BlockStarted, ArtifactProduced, BlockFinished, RunFinished) carrying config hash, block versions, input/output artifact ids, seed, git commit, timings, host info — v0.1.
  • FR-LIN-2: events go to pluggable lineage sinks; the core ships json (one lineage.json per run in the store, default) — v0.1. SQLite, OpenLineage and MLflow sinks are optional — v0.2+.
  • FR-LIN-3: multiple sinks can be active at once; lineage: off disables lineage entirely (caching still works, since it relies on artifact hashes, not on lineage).
  • FR-LIN-4: secrets are never written to any sink.

docs.title: 4. Non-functional requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement NFR-1 Performance Core overhead per block < 5 ms; independent branches run in parallel. NFR-2 Reproducibility Same config + same input hashes + same seed ⇒ same artifact hashes for deterministic blocks; unchanged nodes are skipped (cache). NFR-3 Portability Linux, macOS, Windows; x86_64 and aarch64. Edge targets armv7. NFR-4 Security No secrets in config files (env/secret-provider references only); plugin sandboxing via WASM; signed artifacts from v0.3. NFR-5 Observability Every run emits structured logs and a lineage record. NFR-6 Stability Semantic versioning; public API of mallops-core frozen at 1.0. MSRV documented and tested in CI. NFR-7 Footprint mallops-core compiles without any ML, cloud-SDK or object_store dependency; only tokio, serde, blake3, tracing.

docs.title: 5. Pipeline definition (mallops.yaml)
docs.text:
version: 1
name: churn-classifier

store:                   # artifact store (optional, this is the default)
  kind: local            # local | memory | s3 | gcs | azure | plugin:<name>
  path: ./.mallops

lineage:                 # optional; default is [{ sink: json }]
  - sink: json
  - sink: openlineage
    with: { url: "${env:OPENLINEAGE_URL}" }
  # lineage: off         # disable completely

blocks:
  raw:
    use: std/ingest.csv
    with:
      path: data/customers.csv

  features:
    use: std/preprocess.tabular
    in: { data: raw.dataset }
    with:
      target: churned
      steps:
        - impute: { strategy: median }
        - scale: { method: standard }
        - split: { test: 0.2, seed: 42 }

  model:
    use: std/train.external            # any language, any library
    in: { train: features.train }
    with:
      command: ["python", "train.py"]
      flavor: sklearn-pickle
      params: { n_estimators: 200 }

  eval:
    use: std/evaluate.classification
    in: { model: model.model, test: features.test }
    with:
      gate: { metric: f1, min: 0.80 }

  package:
    use: std/package
    in: { model: model.model, preprocess: features.transform, metrics: eval.metrics }

  serve:
    use: std/serve.http
    in: { package: package.package }
    with: { port: 8080 }

Rules: - use references a block by namespace/name (std/… built-in, plugin/… installed plugin, wasm:path.wasm, grpc:host:port). - in wires named inputs to <block>.<output>; this defines the DAG. Cycles are rejected. - with is block-specific config, validated against the block's JSON schema. - Values may reference environment variables ${env:NAME} and secrets ${secret:NAME}; secrets are never written to lineage. - A JSON Schema for the file is generated from Rust types (schemars) and published for editor completion.

docs.title: 6. Artifact contract
docs.text:
<store>/artifacts/<blake3-hash>/
├── manifest.json
└── payload/…          # any files, opaque to the core

{
  "kind": "model",
  "format": "pickle",
  "flavor": "sklearn-pickle",
  "signature": { "inputs": [{"name": "age", "dtype": "f64"}], "outputs": [{"name": "churned", "dtype": "f64"}] },
  "metadata": { "framework": "scikit-learn", "framework_version": "1.6.0" },
  "produced_by": { "run": "01J…", "block": "model" },
  "parents": ["<hash>", "<hash>"]
}
kind Typical format values Notes dataset parquet, arrow-ipc, csv, json, images, tfrecord, any Arrow/Parquet is the interchange default for std blocks only features as dataset plus optional fitted transform artifact model onnx, safetensors, torchscript, pickle, joblib, gguf, xgboost-json, savedmodel, any flavor selects the predictor metrics json key → number map + optional plots package dir, oci model + transforms + manifest blob any escape hatch

Inputs and outputs of blocks declare the accepted kind and optionally accepted formats / flavors; mallops validate checks compatibility before running.

docs.title: 7. Roadmap
docs.text: Version Scope v0.1 mallops-core (Block trait, artifacts, ArtifactStore + local/memory, lineage events + JSON sink, DAG runtime, YAML), CLI (init, validate, run, graph, blocks list, serve), std blocks: ingest csv/parquet, preprocess tabular, train linfa + external, evaluate classification/regression, package, serve http v0.2 remote store backends, SQLite/OpenLineage/MLflow lineage sinks, data storage blocks, model registry & versioning, hyperparameter search, deploy local/docker, gRPC serving, OCI packaging v0.3 monitoring (Prometheus/OTel), drift detection, retrain triggers, DL training (burn/candle), signing, canary/shadow deploy v0.4 mallops-edge, federated learning, fleet deploy, distributed monitoring v1.0 stable public API, plugin protocol v1 frozen

docs.title: 8. Open questions
docs.text:
• Plugin discovery/distribution: crates.io-style index vs. OCI registry for WASM/gRPC plugins.
  • Python SDK for writing external blocks (thin package implementing the protocol) — likely v0.2.
  • Which lineage sink becomes the recommended default for querying (SQLite vs. OpenLineage backend) once registries need search.

docs.title: Contributing to mallops
docs.text: Thanks for your interest! Read docs/SPEC.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md first.

Branch From Into Merge style feature/*, fix/*, docs/* dev dev squash release/X.Y.Z dev (via Start release workflow) main merge commit hotfix/X.Y.Z main main merge commit back-merge PR main dev merge commit
  • main contains only released versions; dev is the default branch.
  • Each push on release/* publishes a pre-release vX.Y.Z-beta.N.
  • A hotfix/* branch must bump the patch version in Cargo.toml and update CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Commits and PR titles
docs.text: PRs are squash-merged, so the PR title becomes the commit and must follow Conventional Commits: feat(core): add artifact store, fix(cli): …, docs: …, refactor: …, test: …, ci: …, build: …, chore: …. Breaking changes: feat!: … or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

docs.title: Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)
docs.text:
Every commit must be signed off, certifying that you wrote it or otherwise have the right to submit it under the project license, as stated in the Developer Certificate of Origin. The sign-off is a trailer matching the commit author:

Signed-off-by: Jane Doe <jane@example.com>

Add it with git commit -s. To fix commits already in a PR:

git rebase --signoff origin/dev        # adds the trailer to every commit of the branch
git push --force-with-lease

The dco CI job blocks PRs with unsigned commits (bots and merge commits are exempt). Squash merges keep all trailers in the final commit.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs Material from docs/ and published on GitHub Pages, versioned with mike: /dev/ follows the dev branch, /X.Y/ is published at each release, /latest/ points to the newest stable one.

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve          # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # what CI runs on PRs

The Rust API reference is generated by rustdoc and hosted on docs.rs.

docs.title: Releasing (maintainers)
docs.text:
1. Actions → Start release → choose patch|minor|major. This opens release/X.Y.Z → main and publishes vX.Y.Z-beta.1.
  2. Test the beta; push fixes to the release branch (each push = new beta).
  3. Merge the PR with Create a merge commit. The tag, GitHub Release, binaries and crates.io publish happen automatically.
  4. Merge the auto-opened back-merge PR into dev (merge commit).

Required repository secrets: RELEASE_TOKEN (fine-grained PAT with contents + pull-requests write, so bot-created branches/PRs trigger CI) and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (crates.io).

docs.title: Architecture changes
docs.text: Significant design changes need an ADR in docs/adr/ submitted with or before the implementation.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
Format: MADR light. One decision per file, numbered, never edited after acceptance — supersede with a new ADR instead.

# Title Status 0001 Modular Cargo workspace Accepted 0002 Arrow/Parquet as default (not mandatory) data interchange Accepted 0003 Plugins via WASM components and external processes Accepted 0004 Format-agnostic artifacts with flavors Accepted 0005 GitFlow branching and automated releases Accepted 0006 Artifact store and lineage: contracts in the core, implementations pluggable Accepted

docs.title: 0001 — Modular Cargo workspace
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: mallops must be usable as a library, with plugins, or standalone. Users should pay (compile time, binary size, dependencies) only for the blocks they use.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A Cargo workspace with a small number of crates: mallops-core (no ML deps), mallops-std (standard blocks, each behind a feature flag), mallops-cli, and later mallops-edge. Crates are created only when they have code.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• cargo add mallops-std --features train-linfa,serve-http gives exactly what is needed.
  • Fewer crates = simpler releases. If mallops-std grows too heavy, per-stage crates can be split out without breaking users (re-exports).

docs.title: 0002 — Arrow/Parquet as default (not mandatory) data interchange
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Standard blocks need a common tabular representation to interoperate. At the same time mallops must not lock users into one data format.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Standard tabular blocks exchange data as Parquet files (on disk) and Arrow RecordBatch (in memory). This is a convention of mallops-std, not of the core: a dataset artifact can have any format, and blocks declare which formats they accept.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Zero-copy interop with Polars, DataFusion, DuckDB, pandas/pyarrow in external blocks.
  • Non-tabular data (images, audio, text corpora) flows as plain files with a declared format.
  • Format conversion is an explicit block, never implicit.

docs.title: 0003 — Plugins via WASM components and external processes
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Users need to add blocks without recompiling mallops, often in languages other than Rust (Python dominates ML). Rust has no stable ABI, so dylib plugins break across compiler versions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Three plugin kinds, all exposed to the runtime through the same Block trait: 1. Native: Rust crates registered at compile time (inventory). 2. WASM components (wasmtime, WIT interface) for portable, sandboxed blocks. 3. External processes via a file-based CLI contract (inputs.json/config.json → outputs.json) and, for long-lived workers, a gRPC protocol.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any language works through the external contract; a thin Python SDK is planned.
  • No dylib loading, no ABI issues.
  • The WIT and protobuf definitions become public API and are versioned with the core.

docs.title: 0004 — Format-agnostic artifacts with flavors
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ML teams use many model formats (ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle/joblib, GGUF, XGBoost JSON, SavedModel, custom). Picking one (e.g. ONNX) would exclude models that cannot be converted and force lossy conversions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: An artifact is opaque payload files plus a manifest.json with kind, format, flavor and free-form metadata. The core never reads payloads. Model consumers (serving, evaluation, edge) select an implementation of the Predictor trait by flavor. Backends (ort, tract, candle, burn, linfa, llama.cpp, external Python workers…) are all equal plugins.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any model, any library, any language.
  • Validation is limited to declared metadata; a block that receives an unsupported flavor fails early at mallops validate.
  • Conversions (e.g. torch → onnx) are explicit model-engineering blocks.

docs.title: 0005 — GitFlow branching and automated releases
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project needs a clear contribution flow, stable releases, and a way to ship pre-releases for testing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• main: only released code; every commit is a tag vX.Y.Z.
  • dev: default branch, integration of feature/* and fix/* via PR.
  • release/X.Y.Z: cut from dev by the Start release workflow; every push publishes a GitHub pre-release vX.Y.Z-beta.N. It acts as the beta channel, so no extra long-lived beta branch.
  • hotfix/*: from main, merged back to main and dev.
  • Conventional Commits enforced on PR titles (squash merge); changelog generated by git-cliff.
  • Merge of a release/hotfix PR into main tags, creates the GitHub Release with binaries, publishes crates, and opens a back-merge PR into dev.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One click to start a release, zero manual tagging.
  • Squash merges keep history linear and changelog accurate.

docs.title: 0006 — Artifact store and lineage: contracts in the core, implementations pluggable
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-21
  • Refines: 0001

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The first draft put the artifact store (on top of object_store) and the lineage store inside mallops-core. That contradicts the "small core, optional everything else" principle and drags cloud dependencies into every build.

Two alternatives were considered: 1. Make them blocks. Rejected: blocks are nodes of the DAG, while store and lineage act on every edge. If storage were an optional node, the runtime could not hand data from A to B, and caching/resume would depend on the user remembering to add it. Lineage needs the whole graph, which only the runtime sees; a block would have to rebuild it. 2. Keep full implementations in the core. Rejected: forces object_store and a lineage backend on every user.

The draft also mixed two different things: the data storage lifecycle stage (persisting user data) and the internal artifact store.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The core defines the contracts: ArtifactStore and LineageSink traits, plus the LineageEvent type emitted by the runtime.
  • The core ships only minimal, dependency-free implementations: LocalStore (filesystem, default), MemoryStore (ephemeral), JsonSink (one lineage.json per run).
  • Remote stores (S3, GCS, Azure via object_store) and other lineage sinks (SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow) are mallops-std features or plugins.
  • Lineage supports zero or more sinks; lineage: off disables it. Sink failures are warnings, never run failures.
  • "Data storage" as a lifecycle stage is an ordinary optional block that writes user data to external systems; it is unrelated to the artifact store.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• mallops-core has no cloud or database dependency.
  • Caching, resume and data hand-off always work, because the store mechanism cannot be removed — only its backend swapped.
  • Caching relies on artifact hashes, not lineage, so disabling lineage loses audit history but not performance.
  • ArtifactStore, LineageSink and LineageEvent become public API and must stay stable from 1.0.
